target: User Pi 4B microSD, inspected read-only on macOS
inspection: diskutil list external and diskutil info on the ZEALPI media; mounted the FAT32 volume for a directory listing, then unmounted it
result: The 196.9 GB card currently has an MBR (FDisk) partition table with one FAT32 partition named ZEALPI spanning the card. No second data partition or unallocated tail is present.
mount_note: The mount command did not expose the volume as read-only despite the readOnly argument. No intentional file writes were made; the volume was unmounted immediately after listing. No partitioning or formatting occurred.
implications: The existing Pi firmware/boot FAT32 volume must be preserved.
A separate RedSea data partition requires a partition-layout change, which means backing up and shrinking/rebuilding the full-card FAT32 layout first.
No Pi writable block or filesystem path is accepted yet; this inspection does not test reads or writes from ZealOS.
recommended_direction: Keep the FAT32 boot volume and target a separate native RedSea data partition for ZealOS persistence. USB storage can remain a later optional data target.
scope_note: Host-side card layout and directory listing only. No partitioning, formatting, boot, or intentional filesystem write was performed.
